title: Everything you think you know about addiction is wrong | Johann Hari | TED

blocks.en_text: One of my earliest memories
blocks.zh_text: 我最早的记忆之一

blocks.en_text: is of trying to wake up one of my relatives and not being able to.
blocks.zh_text: 就是试图叫醒我的一个亲戚，却怎么也叫不醒。

blocks.en_text: And I was just a little kid, so I didn't really understand why,
blocks.zh_text: 我当时还只是个小孩子，所以不太明白为什么，

blocks.en_text: but as I got older,
blocks.zh_text: 但随着我长大，

blocks.en_text: I realized we had drug addiction in my family,
blocks.zh_text: 我意识到我们家有吸毒成瘾的问题，

blocks.en_text: including later cocaine addiction.
blocks.zh_text: 后来还包括可卡因成瘾。

blocks.en_text: I'd been thinking about it a lot lately, partly because it's now exactly 100 years
blocks.zh_text: 最近我一直在反复思考这件事，部分原因是现在正好是100年

blocks.en_text: since drugs were first banned in the United States and Britain,
blocks.zh_text: 自从毒品在美国和英国首次被禁止，

blocks.en_text: and we then imposed that on the rest of the world.
blocks.zh_text: 然后我们又把这个禁令强加给了世界其他地方。

blocks.en_text: It's a century since we made this really fateful decision
blocks.zh_text: 距离我们做出这个极其重大的决定已经一个世纪了

blocks.en_text: to take addicts and punish them and make them suffer,
blocks.zh_text: 就是把成瘾者抓起来惩罚他们、让他们受苦，

blocks.en_text: because we believed that would deter them; it would give them an incentive to stop.
blocks.zh_text: 因为我们相信那样能震慑他们，能给他们一个停下来的动力。

blocks.en_text: And a few years ago, I was looking at some of the addicts in my life who I love,
blocks.zh_text: 几年前，我看着生活中我爱的那些成瘾者，

blocks.en_text: and trying to figure out if there was some way to help them.
blocks.zh_text: 想弄清楚有没有什么办法能帮到他们。

blocks.en_text: And I realized there were loads of incredibly basic questions
blocks.zh_text: 然后我意识到，有好多极其基本的问题

blocks.en_text: I just didn't know the answer to,
blocks.zh_text: 我根本不知道答案，

blocks.en_text: like, what really causes addiction?
blocks.zh_text: 比如，到底是什么导致了成瘾？

blocks.en_text: Why do we carry on with this approach that doesn't seem to be working,
blocks.zh_text: 为什么我们还在沿用这种似乎并不奏效的做法，

blocks.en_text: and is there a better way out there that we could try instead?
blocks.zh_text: 有没有更好的办法，我们可以换一种方式试试？

blocks.en_text: So I read loads of stuff about it,
blocks.zh_text: 所以我读了大量关于这方面的资料，

blocks.en_text: and I couldn't really find the answers I was looking for,
blocks.zh_text: 却没能真正找到我想要的答案，

blocks.en_text: so I thought, okay, I'll go and sit with different people around the world
blocks.zh_text: 于是我想，好吧，我要去和世界各地不同的人坐下来聊聊

blocks.en_text: who lived this and studied this
blocks.zh_text: 那些亲身经历过、也研究过这件事的人

blocks.en_text: and talk to them and see if I could learn from them.
blocks.zh_text: 跟他们交谈，看看能不能从他们身上学到东西。

blocks.en_text: And I didn't realize I would end up going over 30,000 miles at the start,
blocks.zh_text: 我没想到一开始就得跑三万多英里，

blocks.en_text: but I ended up going and meeting loads of different people,
blocks.zh_text: 但最后我确实去了，见了许许多多不同的人，

blocks.en_text: from a transgender crack dealer in Brownsville, Brooklyn,
blocks.zh_text: 从布鲁克林布朗斯维尔的一个跨性别快克贩子，

blocks.en_text: to a scientist who spends a lot of time feeding hallucinogens to mongooses
blocks.zh_text: 到一位花大量时间给猫鼬喂致幻剂的科学家

blocks.en_text: to see if they like them --
blocks.zh_text: 看它们喜不喜欢——

blocks.en_text: it turns out they do, but only in very specific circumstances --
blocks.zh_text: 结果发现它们喜欢，但只在非常特定的情况下——

blocks.en_text: to the only country that's ever decriminalized all drugs,
blocks.zh_text: 再到唯一一个把所有毒品都非罪化的国家，

blocks.en_text: from cannabis to crack, Portugal.
blocks.zh_text: 从大麻到快克，那就是葡萄牙。

blocks.en_text: And the thing I realized that really blew my mind is,
blocks.zh_text: 而我意识到的一件事真的让我大为震惊，

blocks.en_text: almost everything we think we know about addiction is wrong,
blocks.zh_text: 那就是我们对成瘾自以为知道的一切几乎都是错的，

blocks.en_text: and if we start to absorb the new evidence about addiction,
blocks.zh_text: 如果我们开始接受关于成瘾的新证据，

blocks.en_text: I think we're going to have to change a lot more than our drug policies.
blocks.zh_text: 我觉得我们要改变的远不止毒品政策。

blocks.en_text: But let's start with what we think we know, what I thought I knew.
blocks.zh_text: 但咱们先从我们自以为知道的事说起，从我以为自己知道的事说起。

blocks.en_text: Let's think about this middle row here.
blocks.zh_text: 咱们来看看中间这一排。

blocks.en_text: Imagine all of you, for 20 days now, went off and used heroin three times a day.
blocks.zh_text: 想象一下，你们所有人，从现在起连续20天，每天吸三次海洛因。

blocks.en_text: Some of you look a little more enthusiastic than others at this prospect.
blocks.zh_text: 有些人看起来比其他人对这个设想更来劲。

blocks.en_text: Don't worry, it's just a thought experiment.
blocks.zh_text: 别担心，这只是个思想实验。

blocks.en_text: Imagine you did that, right?
blocks.zh_text: 想象你们真这么做了，对吧？

blocks.en_text: What would happen?
blocks.zh_text: 会发生什么？

blocks.en_text: Now, we have a story about what would happen that we've been told for a century.
blocks.zh_text: 关于会发生什么，我们有一个讲了一百年的说法。

blocks.en_text: We think, because there are chemical hooks in heroin,
blocks.zh_text: 我们以为，因为海洛因里有化学钩子，

blocks.en_text: as you took it for a while,
blocks.zh_text: 你吸了一段时间之后，

blocks.en_text: your body would become dependent on those hooks,
blocks.zh_text: 你的身体就会依赖上这些钩子，

blocks.en_text: you'd start to physically need them,
blocks.zh_text: 你会开始从生理上需要它们，

blocks.en_text: and at the end of those 20 days, you'd all be heroin addicts. Right?
blocks.zh_text: 那20天结束时，你们就全都成了海洛因瘾君子。对吧？

blocks.en_text: That's what I thought.
blocks.zh_text: 我当时就是这么想的。

blocks.en_text: First thing that alerted me to the fact that something's not right with this story
blocks.zh_text: 最早让我警觉到这个说法有问题的事，

blocks.en_text: is when it was explained to me.
blocks.zh_text: 是别人给我解释的时候。

blocks.en_text: If I step out of this TED Talk today and I get hit by a car and I break my hip,
blocks.zh_text: 如果我今天走出这个TED演讲，被车撞了，摔断了髋骨，

blocks.en_text: I'll be taken to hospital and I'll be given loads of diamorphine.
blocks.zh_text: 我会被送进医院，然后被注射大量二乙酰吗啡。

blocks.en_text: Diamorphine is heroin.
blocks.zh_text: 二乙酰吗啡就是海洛因。

blocks.en_text: It's actually much better heroin than you're going to buy on the streets,
blocks.zh_text: 它其实比你在街上买到的海洛因好得多，

blocks.en_text: because the stuff you buy from a drug dealer is contaminated.
blocks.zh_text: 因为你从毒贩那儿买的东西是掺假的。

blocks.en_text: Actually, very little of it is heroin,
blocks.zh_text: 实际上里面几乎没多少海洛因，

blocks.en_text: whereas the stuff you get from the doctor is medically pure.
blocks.zh_text: 而医生给你的东西是医学上纯净的。

blocks.en_text: And you'll be given it for quite a long period of time.
blocks.zh_text: 而且你会被注射相当长一段时间。

blocks.en_text: There are loads of people in this room,
blocks.zh_text: 这个房间里有很多人，

blocks.en_text: you may not realize it, you've taken quite a lot of heroin.
blocks.zh_text: 你可能没意识到，你们已经摄入过不少海洛因了。

blocks.en_text: And anyone who is watching this anywhere in the world, this is happening.
blocks.zh_text: 全世界任何地方正在看这个演讲的人，这种事都在发生。

blocks.en_text: And if what we believe about addiction is right --
blocks.zh_text: 如果我们对成瘾的看法是对的——

blocks.en_text: those people are exposed to all those chemical hooks --
blocks.zh_text: 那些人接触了所有这些化学钩子——

blocks.en_text: What should happen? They should become addicts.
blocks.zh_text: 那应该会怎样？他们应该会成瘾。

blocks.en_text: This has been studied really carefully.
blocks.zh_text: 这件事被非常仔细地研究过。

blocks.en_text: It doesn't happen; you will have noticed if your grandmother had a hip replacement,
blocks.zh_text: 但并没有发生；如果你奶奶做过髋关节置换，你肯定注意到了，

blocks.en_text: she didn't come out as a junkie. (Laughter)
blocks.zh_text: 她出院时并没有变成瘾君子。（笑声）

blocks.en_text: And when I learned this, it seemed so weird to me,
blocks.zh_text: 当我了解到这一点时，我觉得太奇怪了，

blocks.en_text: so contrary to everything I'd been told, everything I thought I knew,
blocks.zh_text: 跟我被告知的一切、跟我以为自己知道的一切都那么相悖，

blocks.en_text: I just thought it couldn't be right, until I met a man called Bruce Alexander.
blocks.zh_text: 我总觉得这不对劲，直到我遇到一个叫Bruce Alexander的人。

blocks.en_text: He's a professor of psychology in Vancouver
blocks.zh_text: 他是温哥华的一位心理学教授

blocks.en_text: who carried out an incredible experiment
blocks.zh_text: 他做过一个不可思议的实验

blocks.en_text: I think really helps us to understand this issue.
blocks.zh_text: 我觉得这个实验真的能帮我们理解这个问题。

blocks.en_text: Professor Alexander explained to me,
blocks.zh_text: Alexander教授跟我解释说，

blocks.en_text: the idea of addiction we've all got in our heads, that story,
blocks.zh_text: 我们脑子里关于上瘾的那套观念，那个说法，

blocks.en_text: comes partly from a series of experiments
blocks.zh_text: 有一部分来自一系列实验

blocks.en_text: that were done earlier in the 20th century.
blocks.zh_text: 这些实验是20世纪早期做的。

blocks.en_text: They're really simple.
blocks.zh_text: 实验特别简单。

blocks.en_text: You can do them tonight at home if you feel a little sadistic.
blocks.zh_text: 你要是有点虐待倾向，今晚在家就能做。

blocks.en_text: You get a rat and you put it in a cage, and you give it two water bottles:
blocks.zh_text: 你拿一只老鼠，把它放进笼子里，给它两个水瓶：

blocks.en_text: One is just water, and the other is water laced with either heroin or cocaine.
blocks.zh_text: 一个是纯水，另一个是掺了海洛因或可卡因的水。

blocks.en_text: If you do that, the rat will almost always prefer the drug water
blocks.zh_text: 这么做的话，老鼠几乎总是更喜欢那瓶药水

blocks.en_text: and almost always kill itself quite quickly.
blocks.zh_text: 而且几乎总是很快就把自己弄死了。

blocks.en_text: So there you go, right? That's how we think it works.
blocks.zh_text: 你看，对吧？我们以为上瘾就是这么回事。

blocks.en_text: In the '70s, Professor Alexander comes along and he looks at this experiment
blocks.zh_text: 到了70年代，Alexander教授出现了，他看了看这个实验

blocks.en_text: and he noticed something.
blocks.zh_text: 然后注意到了点什么。

blocks.en_text: He said ah, we're putting the rat in an empty cage.
blocks.zh_text: 他说，啊，我们把老鼠放进了一个空笼子里。

blocks.en_text: It's got nothing to do except use these drugs.
blocks.zh_text: 它除了用这些药，没别的事可做。

blocks.en_text: Let's try something different.
blocks.zh_text: 咱们换个方式试试。

blocks.en_text: So Professor Alexander built a cage that he called "Rat Park,"
blocks.zh_text: 于是Alexander教授造了一个笼子，他管它叫“老鼠乐园”，

blocks.en_text: which is basically heaven for rats.
blocks.zh_text: 那基本上就是老鼠的天堂。

blocks.en_text: They've got loads of cheese, they've got loads of colored balls,
blocks.zh_text: 里面有好多奶酪，好多彩色的球，

blocks.en_text: they've got loads of tunnels.
blocks.zh_text: 还有好多隧道。

blocks.en_text: Crucially, they've got loads of friends. They can have loads of sex.
blocks.zh_text: 最关键的是，它们有好多朋友。它们可以尽情交配。

blocks.en_text: And they've got both the water bottles, the normal water and the drugged water.
blocks.zh_text: 而且里面也有那两个水瓶，普通水和药水。

blocks.en_text: But here's the fascinating thing:
blocks.zh_text: 但有意思的是：

blocks.en_text: In Rat Park, they don't like the drug water.
blocks.zh_text: 在老鼠乐园里，它们不喜欢那瓶药水。

blocks.en_text: They almost never use it.
blocks.zh_text: 它们几乎从不碰它。

blocks.en_text: None of them ever use it compulsively.
blocks.zh_text: 没有一只是强迫性地去用的。

blocks.en_text: None of them ever overdose.
blocks.zh_text: 也没有一只用药过量。

blocks.en_text: You go from almost 100 percent overdose when they're isolated
blocks.zh_text: 从隔离状态下接近百分之百的过量率

blocks.en_text: to zero percent overdose when they have happy and connected lives.
blocks.zh_text: 变成了拥有快乐、有联结的生活时百分之零的过量率。

blocks.en_text: Now, when he first saw this, Professor Alexander thought,
blocks.zh_text: Alexander教授第一次看到这个结果时想，

blocks.en_text: maybe this is just a thing about rats, they're quite different to us.
blocks.zh_text: 也许这只是老鼠的情况，它们跟我们挺不一样的。

blocks.en_text: Maybe not as different as we'd like, but, you know --
blocks.zh_text: 也许没我们想的那么不一样，但是，你知道——

blocks.en_text: But fortunately, there was a human experiment
blocks.zh_text: 但幸运的是，有一项人类实验

blocks.en_text: into the exact same principle happening at the exact same time.
blocks.zh_text: 研究的是完全相同的原理，而且恰好发生在同一时期。

blocks.en_text: It was called the Vietnam War.
blocks.zh_text: 它叫越南战争。

blocks.en_text: In Vietnam, 20 percent of all American troops were using loads of heroin,
blocks.zh_text: 在越南，百分之二十的美军士兵大量使用海洛因，

blocks.en_text: and if you look at the news reports from the time,
blocks.zh_text: 如果你看看当时的新闻报道，

blocks.en_text: they were really worried, because they thought, my God, we're going to have
blocks.zh_text: 他们真的非常担心，因为他们想，天哪，我们会有

blocks.en_text: hundreds of thousands of junkies on the streets of the United States
blocks.zh_text: 成千上万的瘾君子出现在美国街头，

blocks.en_text: when the war ends; it made total sense.
blocks.zh_text: 等战争结束的时候；这完全说得通。

blocks.en_text: Now, those soldiers who were using loads of heroin were followed home.
blocks.zh_text: 后来，那些大量使用海洛因的士兵被跟踪调查到了家里。

blocks.en_text: The Archives of General Psychiatry did a really detailed study,
blocks.zh_text: 《普通精神病学档案》做了一项非常详细的研究，

blocks.en_text: and what happened to them?
blocks.zh_text: 他们后来怎么样了呢？

blocks.en_text: It turns out they didn't go to rehab. They didn't go into withdrawal.
blocks.zh_text: 结果他们并没有去戒毒所。他们也没有出现戒断反应。

blocks.en_text: Ninety-five percent of them just stopped.
blocks.zh_text: 其中百分之九十五的人就这么停了。

blocks.en_text: Now, if you believe the story about chemical hooks,
blocks.zh_text: 那么，如果你相信关于化学成瘾钩子的说法，

blocks.en_text: that makes absolutely no sense, but Professor Alexander began to think
blocks.zh_text: 这完全说不通，但Alexander教授开始思考

blocks.en_text: there might be a different story about addiction.
blocks.zh_text: 关于成瘾也许有另一种解释。

blocks.en_text: He said, what if addiction isn't about your chemical hooks?
blocks.zh_text: 他说，如果成瘾跟你的化学钩子无关呢？

blocks.en_text: What if addiction is about your cage?
blocks.zh_text: 如果成瘾跟你的笼子有关呢？

blocks.en_text: What if addiction is an adaptation to your environment?
blocks.zh_text: 如果成瘾是对你所在环境的一种适应呢？

blocks.en_text: Looking at this,
blocks.zh_text: 看到这一点，

blocks.en_text: there was another professor called Peter Cohen in the Netherlands
blocks.zh_text: 荷兰还有一位教授叫Peter Cohen

blocks.en_text: who said, maybe we shouldn't even call it addiction.
blocks.zh_text: 他说，也许我们根本不该把它叫做成瘾。

blocks.en_text: Maybe we should call it bonding.
blocks.zh_text: 也许我们应该把它叫做建立联结。

blocks.en_text: Human beings have a natural and innate need to bond,
blocks.zh_text: 人类有一种天然的、与生俱来的建立联结的需求，

blocks.en_text: and when we're happy and healthy, we'll bond and connect with each other,
blocks.zh_text: 当我们快乐健康的时候，我们会彼此建立联结和联系，

blocks.en_text: but if you can't do that,
blocks.zh_text: 但如果你做不到这一点，

blocks.en_text: because you're traumatized or isolated or beaten down by life,
blocks.zh_text: 因为你受过创伤、被孤立，或者被生活击垮了，

blocks.en_text: you will bond with something that will give you some sense of relief.
blocks.zh_text: 你就会和某种能给你一些解脱感的东西建立联结。

blocks.en_text: Now, that might be gambling, that might be pornography,
blocks.zh_text: 那可能是赌博，可能是色情，

blocks.en_text: that might be cocaine, that might be cannabis,
blocks.zh_text: 可能是可卡因，可能是大麻，

blocks.en_text: but you will bond and connect with something because that's our nature.
blocks.zh_text: 但你会和某种东西建立联结和联系，因为这就是我们的天性。

blocks.en_text: That's what we want as human beings.
blocks.zh_text: 这就是我们作为人类所想要的。

blocks.en_text: And at first, I found this quite a difficult thing to get my head around,
blocks.zh_text: 一开始，我觉得这件事很难理解，

blocks.en_text: but one way that helped me to think about it is,
blocks.zh_text: 但有一个方法帮我理解了它，

blocks.en_text: I can see, I've got over by my seat a bottle of water, right?
blocks.zh_text: 你看，我座位旁边有一瓶水，对吧？

blocks.en_text: I'm looking at lots of you, and lots of you have bottles of water with you.
blocks.zh_text: 我看着你们很多人，你们很多人身边都带着水瓶。

blocks.en_text: Forget the drugs. Forget the drug war.
blocks.zh_text: 先别管毒品。先别管毒品战争。

blocks.en_text: Totally legally, all of those bottles of water could be bottles of vodka, right?
blocks.zh_text: 完全合法地说，所有这些水瓶都可以是伏特加，对吧？

blocks.en_text: We could all be getting drunk -- I might after this -- (Laughter) --
blocks.zh_text: 我们都可以喝醉——我说完这场也许就会——（笑声）——

blocks.en_text: but we're not.
blocks.zh_text: 但我们没有。

blocks.en_text: Now, because you've been able to afford the approximately gazillion pounds
blocks.zh_text: 那么，因为你们能负担得起大约天文数字的英镑

blocks.en_text: that it costs to get into a TED Talk, I'm guessing you guys could afford
blocks.zh_text: 也就是参加一场TED演讲所需的费用，我猜你们应该能负担得起

blocks.en_text: to be drinking vodka for the next six months.
blocks.zh_text: 接下来六个月里一直喝伏特加。

blocks.en_text: You wouldn't end up homeless.
blocks.zh_text: 你不会最终流落街头。

blocks.en_text: You're not going to do that, and the reason you're not going to do that
blocks.zh_text: 你不会那么做，而你不那么做的原因

blocks.en_text: is not because anyone's stopping you.
blocks.zh_text: 并不是因为有人在阻止你。

blocks.en_text: It's because you've got bonds and connections
blocks.zh_text: 而是因为你有牵挂和联系

blocks.en_text: that you want to be present for.
blocks.zh_text: 你希望能陪在它们身边。

blocks.en_text: You've got work you love. You've got people you love.
blocks.zh_text: 你有你热爱的工作。你有你爱的人。

blocks.en_text: You've got healthy relationships.
blocks.zh_text: 你有健康的人际关系。

blocks.en_text: And a core part of addiction,
blocks.zh_text: 而上瘾的一个核心部分，

blocks.en_text: I came to think, and I believe the evidence suggests,
blocks.zh_text: 我逐渐认为，而且我相信证据也表明，

blocks.en_text: is about not being able to bear to be present in your life.
blocks.zh_text: 就是无法忍受活在当下、面对自己的生活。

blocks.en_text: Now, this has really significant implications.
blocks.zh_text: 这有着非常重大的意义。

blocks.en_text: The most obvious implications are for the War on Drugs.
blocks.zh_text: 最明显的意义是针对禁毒战争的。

blocks.en_text: In Arizona, I went out with a group of women
blocks.zh_text: 在亚利桑那州，我和一群女性一起外出

blocks.en_text: who were made to wear t-shirts saying, "I was a drug addict,"
blocks.zh_text: 她们被迫穿着写有“我曾是吸毒者”的T恤

blocks.en_text: and go out on chain gangs and dig graves while members of the public jeer at them,
blocks.zh_text: 出去参加囚犯劳动队挖坟墓，而公众在一旁嘲笑她们，

blocks.en_text: and when those women get out of prison, they're going to have criminal records
blocks.zh_text: 当这些女性出狱后，她们会有犯罪记录

blocks.en_text: that mean they'll never work in the legal economy again.
blocks.zh_text: 这意味着她们再也无法在合法经济中工作。

blocks.en_text: Now, that's a very extreme example, obviously, in the case of the chain gang,
blocks.zh_text: 显然，囚犯劳动队这个例子非常极端，

blocks.en_text: but actually almost everywhere in the world
blocks.zh_text: 但实际上，世界上几乎所有地方

blocks.en_text: we treat addicts to some degree like that.
blocks.zh_text: 我们都在某种程度上这样对待成瘾者。

blocks.en_text: We punish them. We shame them. We give them criminal records.
blocks.zh_text: 我们惩罚他们。我们羞辱他们。我们给他们留下犯罪记录。

blocks.en_text: We put barriers between them reconnecting.
blocks.zh_text: 我们在他们重新建立联系的道路上设置障碍。

blocks.en_text: There was a doctor in Canada, Dr. Gabor Maté, an amazing man,
blocks.zh_text: 加拿大有一位医生，加博尔·马泰医生，一个了不起的人，

blocks.en_text: who said to me, if you wanted to design a system that would make addiction worse,
blocks.zh_text: 他对我说，如果你想设计一个让上瘾变得更严重的系统，

blocks.en_text: you would design that system.
blocks.zh_text: 你就会设计出那样的系统。

blocks.en_text: Now, there's a place that decided to do the exact opposite,
blocks.zh_text: 有一个地方决定做完全相反的事，

blocks.en_text: and I went there to see how it worked.
blocks.zh_text: 我去那里看看它是怎么运作的。

blocks.en_text: In the year 2000, Portugal had one of the worst drug problems in Europe.
blocks.zh_text: 2000年，葡萄牙有着欧洲最严重的毒品问题之一。

blocks.en_text: One percent of the population was addicted to heroin, which is kind of mind-blowing,
blocks.zh_text: 百分之一的人口对海洛因上瘾，这有点令人难以置信，

blocks.en_text: and every year, they tried the American way more and more.
blocks.zh_text: 而且每年，他们都越来越多地尝试美国的方式。

blocks.en_text: They punished people and stigmatized them and shamed them more,
blocks.zh_text: 他们更多地惩罚人们、给他们污名、羞辱他们，

blocks.en_text: and every year, the problem got worse.
blocks.zh_text: 而每年，问题都变得更严重。

blocks.en_text: And one day, the Prime Minister and the leader of the opposition got together,
blocks.zh_text: 有一天，总理和反对党领袖聚在一起，

blocks.en_text: and basically said, look, we can't go on
blocks.zh_text: 基本上说，你看，我们不能再这样下去了

blocks.en_text: with a country where we're having ever more people becoming heroin addicts.
blocks.zh_text: 我们的国家有越来越多的人成为海洛因成瘾者。

blocks.en_text: Let's set up a panel of scientists and doctors
blocks.zh_text: 让我们成立一个由科学家和医生组成的小组

blocks.en_text: to figure out what would genuinely solve the problem.
blocks.zh_text: 来弄清楚什么才能真正解决这个问题。

blocks.en_text: And they set up a panel led by an amazing man called Dr. João Goulão,
blocks.zh_text: 他们成立了一个小组，由一位了不起的人若昂·古朗博士领导，

blocks.en_text: to look at all this new evidence,
blocks.zh_text: 来研究所有这些新证据，

blocks.en_text: and they came back and they said,
blocks.zh_text: 然后他们回来汇报说，

blocks.en_text: "Decriminalize all drugs from cannabis to crack, but" --
blocks.zh_text: “把所有毒品都去罪化，从大麻到快克可卡因，但是”——

blocks.en_text: and this is the crucial next step --
blocks.zh_text: 而这是关键的下一步——

blocks.en_text: "take all the money we used to spend on cutting addicts off,
blocks.zh_text: “把过去用来切断成瘾者、

blocks.en_text: on disconnecting them,
blocks.zh_text: 让他们与社会脱节的钱，

blocks.en_text: and spend it instead on reconnecting them with society."
blocks.zh_text: 转而花在让他们重新与社会建立联系上。”

blocks.en_text: And that's not really what we think of as drug treatment
blocks.zh_text: 而这并不是我们通常认为的戒毒治疗，

blocks.en_text: in the United States and Britain.
blocks.zh_text: 在美国和英国可不是这样。

blocks.en_text: So they do do residential rehab,
blocks.zh_text: 他们确实有住院康复治疗，

blocks.en_text: they do psychological therapy, that does have some value.
blocks.zh_text: 他们做心理治疗，那确实有一定价值。

blocks.en_text: But the biggest thing they did was the complete opposite of what we do:
blocks.zh_text: 但他们做的最重要的事，跟我们的做法完全相反：

blocks.en_text: a massive program of job creation for addicts,
blocks.zh_text: 一个为成瘾者创造就业的大规模项目，

blocks.en_text: and microloans for addicts to set up small businesses.
blocks.zh_text: 还有为成瘾者提供小额贷款去创业。

blocks.en_text: So say you used to be a mechanic.
blocks.zh_text: 比如说你以前是个机械师。

blocks.en_text: When you're ready, they'll go to a garage, and they'll say,
blocks.zh_text: 等你准备好了，他们会去一家修车厂，说，

blocks.en_text: if you employ this guy for a year, we'll pay half his wages.
blocks.zh_text: 如果你雇这个人一年，我们付他一半的工资。

blocks.en_text: The goal was to make sure that every addict in Portugal
blocks.zh_text: 目标是确保葡萄牙的每一个成瘾者

blocks.en_text: had something to get out of bed for in the morning.
blocks.zh_text: 早上都有个起床的理由。

blocks.en_text: And when I went and met the addicts in Portugal,
blocks.zh_text: 当我去葡萄牙见到那些成瘾者时，

blocks.en_text: what they said is, as they rediscovered purpose,
blocks.zh_text: 他们说，随着他们重新找到目标，

blocks.en_text: they rediscovered bonds and relationships with the wider society.
blocks.zh_text: 他们也重新找到了与更广泛社会的纽带和关系。

blocks.en_text: It'll be 15 years this year since that experiment began,
blocks.zh_text: 到今年，那项实验开始就满15年了，

blocks.en_text: and the results are in:
blocks.zh_text: 结果已经出来了：

blocks.en_text: injecting drug use is down in Portugal,
blocks.zh_text: 在葡萄牙，注射吸毒减少了，

blocks.en_text: according to the British Journal of Criminology,
blocks.zh_text: 根据《英国犯罪学杂志》，

blocks.en_text: by 50 percent, five-zero percent.
blocks.zh_text: 减少了50%，五零，百分之五十。

blocks.en_text: Overdose is massively down, HIV is massively down among addicts.
blocks.zh_text: 用药过量大幅下降，成瘾者中的HIV也大幅下降。

blocks.en_text: Addiction in every study is significantly down.
blocks.zh_text: 每一项研究里，成瘾都显著下降。

blocks.en_text: One of the ways you know it's worked so well is that almost nobody in Portugal
blocks.zh_text: 你知道它效果这么好的一个标志是，葡萄牙几乎没有人

blocks.en_text: wants to go back to the old system.
blocks.zh_text: 想回到旧制度。

blocks.en_text: Now, that's the political implications.
blocks.zh_text: 这就是政治层面的影响。

blocks.en_text: I actually think there's a layer of implications
blocks.zh_text: 其实我认为，在这一切之下还有一层影响，

blocks.en_text: to all this research below that.
blocks.zh_text: 是所有这些研究带来的。

blocks.en_text: We live in a culture where people feel really increasingly vulnerable
blocks.zh_text: 我们生活在一个文化里，人们越来越觉得自己很脆弱，

blocks.en_text: to all sorts of addictions, whether it's to their smartphones
blocks.zh_text: 容易对各种东西上瘾，不管是智能手机

blocks.en_text: or to shopping or to eating.
blocks.zh_text: 还是购物，还是吃东西。

blocks.en_text: Before these talks began -- you guys know this --
blocks.zh_text: 在这次演讲开始之前——你们都知道——

blocks.en_text: we were told we weren't allowed to have our smartphones on,
blocks.zh_text: 我们被告知不许开手机，

blocks.en_text: and I have to say, a lot of you looked an awful lot like
blocks.zh_text: 我得说，你们很多人看起来特别像

blocks.en_text: addicts who were told their dealer was going to be unavailable
blocks.zh_text: 被告知毒贩要断货的成瘾者

blocks.en_text: for the next couple of hours. (Laughter)
blocks.zh_text: 接下来几个小时。（笑声）

blocks.en_text: A lot of us feel like that, and it might sound weird to say,
blocks.zh_text: 我们很多人都这么觉得，说起来可能有点奇怪，

blocks.en_text: I've been talking about how disconnection is a major driver of addiction
blocks.zh_text: 我一直在讲，人与人之间的疏离是成瘾的一大驱动因素

blocks.en_text: and weird to say it's growing,
blocks.zh_text: 说起来也奇怪，这种疏离还在加剧，

blocks.en_text: because you think we're the most connected society that's ever been, surely.
blocks.zh_text: 因为你肯定会想，我们明明是有史以来联系最紧密的社会。

blocks.en_text: But I increasingly began to think that the connections we have
blocks.zh_text: 但我越来越觉得，我们所拥有的联系

blocks.en_text: or think we have, are like a kind of parody of human connection.
blocks.zh_text: 或者说我们自以为拥有的联系，不过是对人际联系的一种拙劣模仿。

blocks.en_text: If you have a crisis in your life, you'll notice something.
blocks.zh_text: 如果你生活中遇到危机，你会发现一件事。

blocks.en_text: It won't be your Twitter followers who come to sit with you.
blocks.zh_text: 来陪你坐着的，不会是你的推特粉丝。

blocks.en_text: It won't be your Facebook friends who help you turn it round.
blocks.zh_text: 帮你扭转局面的，也不会是你的脸书好友。

blocks.en_text: It'll be your flesh and blood friends who you have deep and nuanced
blocks.zh_text: 而是你那些有血有肉的朋友，你和他们有着深厚、细腻

blocks.en_text: and textured, face-to-face relationships with,
blocks.zh_text: 而有质感的面对面关系，

blocks.en_text: and there's a study I learned about from Bill McKibben, the environmental writer,
blocks.zh_text: 我从环境作家比尔·麦吉本那里了解到一项研究，

blocks.en_text: that I think tells us a lot about this.
blocks.zh_text: 我觉得它能很好地说明这一点。

blocks.en_text: It looked at the number of close friends the average American believes
blocks.zh_text: 这项研究调查了普通美国人认为自己

blocks.en_text: they can call on in a crisis.
blocks.zh_text: 在遇到危机时能求助的密友数量。

blocks.en_text: That number has been declining steadily since the 1950s.
blocks.zh_text: 这个数字自20世纪50年代以来一直在稳步下降。

blocks.en_text: The amount of floor space an individual has in their home
blocks.zh_text: 而一个人家里拥有的居住面积

blocks.en_text: has been steadily increasing,
blocks.zh_text: 却一直在稳步增加，

blocks.en_text: and I think that's like a metaphor
blocks.zh_text: 我觉得这就像是一个隐喻，

blocks.en_text: for the choice we've made as a culture.
blocks.zh_text: 象征着我们在文化上所做的选择。

blocks.en_text: We've traded floorspace for friends, we've traded stuff for connections,
blocks.zh_text: 我们用朋友换来了居住面积，用物品换来了联系，

blocks.en_text: and the result is we are one of the loneliest societies there has ever been.
blocks.zh_text: 结果就是我们成了有史以来最孤独的社会之一。

blocks.en_text: And Bruce Alexander, the guy who did the Rat Park experiment, says,
blocks.zh_text: 做过老鼠乐园实验的布鲁斯·亚历山大说，

blocks.en_text: we talk all the time in addiction about individual recovery,
blocks.zh_text: 我们在成瘾问题上总是谈个人康复，

blocks.en_text: and it's right to talk about that,
blocks.zh_text: 谈这个当然没错，

blocks.en_text: but we need to talk much more about social recovery.
blocks.zh_text: 但我们更需要谈社会层面的康复。

blocks.en_text: Something's gone wrong with us, not just with individuals but as a group,
blocks.zh_text: 我们出了问题，不只是个人出了问题，而是整个群体出了问题，

blocks.en_text: and we've created a society where, for a lot of us,
blocks.zh_text: 我们创造了一个社会，在这个社会里，对我们很多人来说，

blocks.en_text: life looks a whole lot more like that isolated cage
blocks.zh_text: 生活更像是那个孤立的笼子，

blocks.en_text: and a whole lot less like Rat Park.
blocks.zh_text: 而远不像老鼠乐园。

blocks.en_text: If I'm honest, this isn't why I went into it.
blocks.zh_text: 说实话，我当初研究这个并不是为了这些。

blocks.en_text: I didn't go in to the discover the political stuff, the social stuff.
blocks.zh_text: 我一开始并不是想发现这些政治层面、社会层面的东西。

blocks.en_text: I wanted to know how to help the people I love.
blocks.zh_text: 我只是想知道该怎么帮助我爱的人。

blocks.en_text: And when I came back from this long journey and I'd learned all this,
blocks.zh_text: 当我走完这段漫长的旅程、学到了这一切之后，

blocks.en_text: I looked at the addicts in my life,
blocks.zh_text: 我看着我生活中那些成瘾的人，

blocks.en_text: and if you're really candid, it's hard loving an addict,
blocks.zh_text: 说实话，爱一个成瘾的人真的很难，

blocks.en_text: and there's going to be lots of people who know in this room.
blocks.zh_text: 在座的很多人都会懂。

blocks.en_text: You are angry a lot of the time,
blocks.zh_text: 你很多时候都在生气，

blocks.en_text: and I think one of the reasons why this debate is so charged
blocks.zh_text: 我觉得这场争论之所以这么激烈，其中一个原因

blocks.en_text: is because it runs through the heart of each of us, right?
blocks.zh_text: 是因为它触及我们每个人的内心，对吧？

blocks.en_text: Everyone has a bit of them that looks at an addict and thinks,
blocks.zh_text: 每个人心里都有一点，看着一个成瘾者会想，

blocks.en_text: I wish someone would just stop you.
blocks.zh_text: 真希望有人能拦住你。

blocks.en_text: And the kind of scripts we're told for how to deal with the addicts in our lives
blocks.zh_text: 而我们被告知的那套应对生活中成瘾者的方法

blocks.en_text: is typified by, I think,
blocks.zh_text: 最典型的代表，我觉得，

blocks.en_text: the reality show "Intervention," if you guys have ever seen it.
blocks.zh_text: 就是真人秀《干预》，你们要是看过的话。

blocks.en_text: I think everything in our lives is defined by reality TV,
blocks.zh_text: 我觉得我们生活里的一切都被真人秀定义了，

blocks.en_text: but that's another TED Talk.
blocks.zh_text: 不过那是另一个TED演讲了。

blocks.en_text: If you've ever seen the show "Intervention,"
blocks.zh_text: 如果你看过《干预》这个节目，

blocks.en_text: it's a pretty simple premise.
blocks.zh_text: 它的设定很简单。

blocks.en_text: Get an addict, all the people in their life, gather them together,
blocks.zh_text: 找一个成瘾者，把他生活里所有的人都聚到一起，

blocks.en_text: confront them with what they're doing, and they say, if you don't shape up,
blocks.zh_text: 当面质问他的所作所为，然后他们说，你要是再不改正，

blocks.en_text: we're going to cut you off.
blocks.zh_text: 我们就跟你断绝关系。

blocks.en_text: So what they do is they take the connection to the addict,
blocks.zh_text: 所以他们做的，就是拿和成瘾者之间的联结

blocks.en_text: and they threaten it, they make it contingent
blocks.zh_text: 来威胁他，让它变成有条件的

blocks.en_text: on the addict behaving the way they want.
blocks.zh_text: 条件就是成瘾者要按他们想要的方式行事。

blocks.en_text: And I began to think, I began to see why that approach doesn't work,
blocks.zh_text: 我开始思考，开始明白为什么这种方法行不通，

blocks.en_text: and I began to think that's almost like the importing of the logic of the Drug War
blocks.zh_text: 我开始觉得，这几乎就像是把禁毒战争的逻辑

blocks.en_text: into our private lives.
blocks.zh_text: 搬进了我们的私人生活。

blocks.en_text: So I was thinking, how could I be Portuguese?
blocks.zh_text: 所以我在想，我怎么能像葡萄牙人那样做呢？

blocks.en_text: And what I've tried to do now, and I can't tell you I do it consistently
blocks.zh_text: 我现在努力去做的，我没法说我做得始终如一

blocks.en_text: and I can't tell you it's easy,
blocks.zh_text: 也没法说这很容易，

blocks.en_text: is to say to the addicts in my life
blocks.zh_text: 就是对我生活里的成瘾者说

blocks.en_text: that I want to deepen the connection with them,
blocks.zh_text: 我想加深和他们的联结，

blocks.en_text: to say to them, I love you whether you're using or you're not.
blocks.zh_text: 对他们说，不管你吸不吸毒，我都爱你。

blocks.en_text: I love you, whatever state you're in,
blocks.zh_text: 我爱你，不管你处于什么状态，

blocks.en_text: and if you need me, I'll come and sit with you
blocks.zh_text: 如果你需要我，我会来陪你坐坐

blocks.en_text: because I love you and I don't want you to be alone
blocks.zh_text: 因为我爱你，我不想让你孤单

blocks.en_text: or to feel alone.
blocks.zh_text: 也不想让你感到孤单。

blocks.en_text: And I think the core of that message --
blocks.zh_text: 我觉得这个信息的核心——

blocks.en_text: you're not alone, we love you --
blocks.zh_text: 你并不孤单，我们爱你——

blocks.en_text: has to be at every level of how we respond to addicts,
blocks.zh_text: 必须贯穿于我们应对成瘾者的每一个层面，

blocks.en_text: socially, politically and individually.
blocks.zh_text: 社会层面、政治层面和个人层面。

blocks.en_text: For 100 years now, we've been singing war songs about addicts.
blocks.zh_text: 一百年来，我们一直在唱关于成瘾者的战歌。

blocks.en_text: I think all along we should have been singing love songs to them,
blocks.zh_text: 我觉得一直以来，我们都应该对他们唱情歌。

blocks.en_text: because the opposite of addiction is not sobriety.
blocks.zh_text: 因为成瘾的反面并不是清醒。

blocks.en_text: The opposite of addiction is connection.
blocks.zh_text: 成瘾的反面是联结。

blocks.en_text: Thank you.
blocks.zh_text: 谢谢。
